name: tabs
description: One region, several panels, one visible at a time. 47 uses across the app and avenID — and none on the website, which is why an earlier pass measured this at zero and left it out. A website-only measurement is not an estate measurement.

list.$description: Scrolls rather than wraps, because a tab strip that wraps to two rows stops reading as one control. A scrolling strip needs a VISIBLE cue that it scrolls — the mask below — since an aria-label mentioning it serves screen readers only and sighted users simply lose the tabs.

selected.$description: Weight and a rule, not colour alone — the underline is what carries the state for anyone who cannot separate the two inks.

a11y.note: The WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, which is a KEYBOARD model before it is a visual one: one stop in the tab order for the whole strip (`tabindex=0` on the selected tab, `-1` on the rest), Left/Right to move between tabs, Home/End to the ends. Each tab carries `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel `aria-labelledby` its tab. A strip of buttons that merely looks like tabs makes every tab a separate tab stop and tells a screen reader nothing about the relationship.
